# AIMN local asset backup and restore\n\nThis utility protects ORBIT's local SQLite memory and generated files in addition to the AIMN PostgreSQL backup. It uses only Python's standard library and does not require Docker.\n\n## Included paths\n\n- `data/` — ORBIT SQLite memory, discovery results, scripts, rendered videos, captions and publishing packages.\n- `media/raw/`, `media/generated/`, `media/final/` — local media folders reserved for source, generated and final assets.\n\nSymbolic links are skipped. Credential-like files such as `.env`, `credentials.json`, `token.json`, and `client_secret*.json` are excluded. Keep OAuth credentials and `.env` separately in encrypted storage; never put them in an archive or Git.\n\n## Commands\n\nRun from the repository root:\n\n```bash\npython scripts/aimn_assets.py backup\npython scripts/aimn_assets.py verify backups/YOUR_ASSET_ARCHIVE.tar.gz\npython scripts/aimn_assets.py restore backups/YOUR_ASSET_ARCHIVE.tar.gz --confirm-add\n```\n\nKeep the `.tar.gz` and matching `.tar.gz.json` manifest together. Verification checks the archive checksum and each file's checksum. Restore requires an interactive confirmation phrase and refuses to overwrite existing files. Restore into a clean destination first; if files already exist, preserve them separately rather than overwriting them.\n\n## Full migration set\n\n1. PostgreSQL: `python scripts/aimn_backup.py backup`\n2. Local ORBIT files: `python scripts/aimn_assets.py backup`\n3. Private configuration: transfer `.env` separately using encrypted storage.\n4. On the new host, restore PostgreSQL and local files, then start Docker Compose.\n\nAIMN agent lessons in PostgreSQL are included in the database dump. ORBIT's standalone `data/orbit.sqlite3` memory is included in this asset archive. This copies memory records; it does not train model weights.
